title.narrative: Science and Technology Project in Upper Secondary Education

description.narrative: The proposed project is part of Asian Development Bank (ADB) strategically sequenced support to harness the transformational potential of upper secondary education (USE) in Cambodia. The project will build on the first two USE programs by deepening reforms in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education and address the increasing demand for high-quality human resources to boost Cambodia's rapidly evolving economy. It will improve upper secondary STEM education by (i) providing high-quality teaching-learning environments in a wide range of upper secondary schools (USSs) nationwide, (ii) increasing the skills of USE STEM teachers and strengthening STEM education delivery, and (iii) strengthening USS leadership and management capacity.

description.narrative: Effectiveness of upper secondary education improved

At least 1.5 percentage point increase in proportion of female and male upper secondary education (USE) science stream students in 50 SRSs passing grade 12 national exam Progress/Status: Status: Ongoing • Same as Q1 2025 Grade 12 exam result percentage shared by Science students (from 50 SRSs): Total 66.76% Female 66.06%
Source: Department of Examination Affairs (2023) AM (Dec 2024) Data Source: MoEYS EMIS and MoEYS Annual Education Congress Reports Actual value:

At least three SRSs accredited as new generation schools with at least 1,400 girls and at least 1,400 boys enrolled Progress/Status: Status: Ongoing • The TOR for the firm to support new NGS expansion is being finalized for submission to the procurement team in July 2025. Data Source: MoEYS EMIS reports Actual value:

At least 2% increase in proportion of secondary resource schools (SRSs) meeting MSS for outputs Progress/Status: Status: Ongoing • Approval of MSS and MTEF is delayed as wider consultation with stakeholders is needed. • Both specialists of MSS and MTEF completed their contracts, but additional inputs from them are needed with revised schedules of the specialists • Approval of the MSS is expected in September 2025. Data Source: MoEYS EMIS reports Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Equitable access to standards-based upper secondary education expanded Indicator: STEM and education technology equipment provided to 258 USSs Progress/Status: The project team (TU1) has cooperated with the Department of State Property and Construction (DSPC) and the procurement unit worked on the provision of STEM and EdTech equipment. The team has prepared and completed key achievement as follows: (i) Renovation of computer rooms in 149 schools: Completed a) an assessment of the locations; b) specification and BoQ, (ii), Providing computers and furniture in 149 schools: a) Bid opened on 30 September 2025, b) the supply firms are being evaluated, (iii) Providing Smart Classrooms to 157 schools: Completed: a) bid document , b) an assessment of the supply firm, (iv) Digital Libraries and STEM supporting teaching materials and 3D printers: Preparing specifications for digital libraries and 3D printers. Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports Actual value:

Output: Equitable access to standards-based upper secondary education expanded Indicator: Upper Secondary Schools (USSs) upgraded with standardized SRS facilities, with gender-responsive, socially inclusive, and climate-adaptive design features Progress/Status: By Q4 2025, (i) Provided contracts: a) package (CW-02) renovation of classroom to be science classroom and library in 122 schools: Awarded the contract on 16 December 2025; b) workshop equipment for 4 general technical high school (GTHS). (ii) Other packages are under the procurement process: a) 25 multi-purpose rooms: Advertising for the firm from 12 November to 17 December 2025, specification of furniture being prepared, bid opened in week 2 of December 2025;, b) supply of laboratory equipment lab material at 122 schools: Complete the bidding of lab materials, and safety equipment; c) scientific equipment and safety equipment, d) books and library materials, d) washing facilities in 18 remaining SRSs and 50 NWS: Prepared BOQ, and drawing/ design;, e) supply of computers, f) Installation of electrical system in102 schools: Prepared BOQ and design/drawing; g) supply of smart classrooms, c) Digital library.
Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for planning, management and delivery of education strengthened Indicator: At least three new USS partnerships on teacher and school director continuous professional development and STEM curriculum implementation established with tertiary and polytechnic education and training institutions, nongovernment organizations, international schools, and industry and business established and implemented Progress/Status: • VOD and PISC developed a Guideline on partnership framework implementation and monitoring CDP and curriculum partnership. • The guideline was approved on 30 June 2025. • VOD has supported five SRS to sign MOUs with TVET and private schools. • An IT expert (ICS-12) to support VOD to review and develop the IT curriculum for GTHS is expected to be mobilized in August 2025
Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for planning, management and delivery of education strengthened Indicator: SRSs operationalize partnerships for joint delivery programs for USS students with gender-responsive professional safety guidelines Progress/Status: • VOD developed Guidelines on school grants implementation and monitoring for joint delivery of different partnerships. • On 27 May 202, the guideline was submitted to MoEYS for approval.
Safety guidelines are to be developed by VOD.
Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for planning, management and delivery of education strengthened Indicator: School directors (at least 80% of available female school directors) report overall increased knowledge and understanding of instructional leadership, partnership building, resource mobilization, and stakeholder engagement Progress/Status: As per the advice of ADB, additional indicators on the minimum percentage of SRSs meeting the SBM (MoSS) effectiveness standards will be added to the DMF at mid-term review.
Key activities: i) Developing a MoSS data management system and updated the tracking system, (ii) Updating key performance indicators (KPI) at the Secretariat of the MoSS, (iv) Continuing to support 259 target schools in implementing MoSS through on-site support and coaching, (v) Prepared baseline and endline assessment reports for the implementation of MoSS, (vi) awarded the contract of International Technical Specialist for School-based Management (SBM)/ MoSS Assessment (ICS-13) and he started working on 13 October 2025. Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports, CSTC reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity for planning, management and delivery of education strengthened Indicator: Technical and education specialists, teachers, provincial and district office education staff, and school directors (at least 40% female) report improved capacity on project implementation, gender-based analysis, and results-based monitoring and evaluation Progress/Status: • Cohort 2: 21 (F=8) education specialists are in the process of recruitment. • The training topics will be on STEM, EMIS, digital education, policy analysis, leadership, communication and soft skills. Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports, pre-and post-surveys Actual value:

Output: Quality of STEM teaching and learning strengthened Indicator: NIE stem lecturers (including at least 80% of available female NIE STEM lecturers) report overall increased knowledge and understanding of effective and innovative teaching strategies, integration of technology into STEM teaching, and increased pedagogical content knowledge Progress/Status: • Two trainings of STEM teacher training to be held in July 2025. o 9- 13 July 2025 in Kampot province o 27- 31 July 2025 in Battambang province o The trainings will be delivered by the 25 NIE STEM lecturers (core trainers)
Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports; review mission reports Actual value:

Output: Quality of STEM teaching and learning strengthened Indicator: USE STEM teachers (at least 40% women) from 50 SRS, 101 SRS network schools, and 4 general technical high schools report overall increased pedagogical content knowledge, understanding of innovative teaching strategies, and integration of technology into STEM teaching, and are engaged in professional learning communities Progress/Status: Key activities: Four rounds of training provided to 413 (F=27%) STEM teacher equal to 53.39% of the target of 775 STEM teachers. Of these trained teachers, 275 (or 66.50%) have fulfilled the requirement to get 3 credits from the CDPMO. Conducted 6 rounds of coached and mentored on scientific experiments/ material for 198 (F=26%) STEM teachers.
Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports; review mission reports, pre- and post-surveys Actual value:

Output: Quality of STEM teaching and learning strengthened Indicator: STEM school-level model action plans for effective teaching, learning, and competency-based student assessment piloted in 30 target USSs Progress/Status: Key activities: Conducted three consultative/ capacity building workshops for 30 target schools and NGS schools
 From 20 to 22 December 2025, in Kampot province: A capacity building workshop on “CBA Summative Assessment” with 211 (F=29) participants. It aimed to (i) share experiences on integrating AI tools for test item generation, (ii) share best practices in developing monthly, quarterly, and semester examinations delivered by science teachers from the NGS, (iii) develop science test items for the monthly exam aligned with CBA. Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports Actual value:

Output: Equitable access to standards-based upper secondary education expanded Indicator: Action plan to harmonize pathways for upper secondary students to the education and technical training programs and certifications based on the Cambodia Qualifications Framework implemented Progress/Status: The current plan may require additional resourcing, given the changing scope of the activity, to be reported on in the next period. It is planned that 50 SRSs and 11 upper secondary schools are to be selected to pilot this new pathway in the next AY 2025-2026. Implementing an action plan to harmonize technical vocational training with general education, scheduled for completion in December 2025.
Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Equitable access to standards-based upper secondary education expanded Indicator: Five-year secondary education medium-term expenditure framework developed, including multi-year budget estimates, and aligned with Cambodia's Secondary Education Blueprint 2030, developed and implemented Progress/Status: Draft MTEF document was prepared and is being reviewed by the Department of Finance (DoF) and the Department of Planning (DoPl) in coordination with technical implementing unit 1 (TIU1). A technical specialist on is to be recruited to help finalize the MTEF, the TORs are being prepared. The MTEF is expected to be completed by 2027 Data Source: MoEYS medium-term expenditure framework document and quarterly project reports Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Quality of STEM teaching and learning strengthened Indicator: Cambodia Science and Technology Center (CSTC) established, fully equipped, staffed, and operational with gender-responsive, climate-smart features and socially inclusive aspects Progress/Status: Key activities: (i) completed the feasibility of the CSTC; (ii) Four field trips of which two were done in Q1 and Q2 and two were done in Q4 2025; (iii) Terms of Reference (ToR) for external consultants are under the recruitment process: An international scientific specialists (ICS-08) and a Detailed Engineering Design (DED) technicians (ICS-05). The TOR of the (CS-05) is being revised STEP UP -Q4 2025 Report 10 the procurement review committee (PRC) while the (ICS-08) is expected to be mobilized in Q1 2026, (iv) The PISC PPP specialist has cooperated with ITC personnel to support industry engagement with CSTC. Data Source: MoEYS quarterly project reports; CSTC reports Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y
